perspective:
**Bradley Ochoa’s available information / subjective record:**

- He knows he is a salesperson at a marketing firm and Katherine Lasiloo is the marketing manager, his colleague. He experiences their professional relationship as cordial but sometimes strained because they disagree on sales vs. marketing strategies.
- In the meeting room, he presented data/charts from the last five campaigns to support his view that traditional sales methods are being overlooked in favor of digital strategies Katherine supports. He told Katherine this. Katherine responded that the market is evolving, that digital outreach potential cannot be ignored, and asked how he reconciles his data with rising online engagement. He clarified he does not want to abandon digital; he is frustrated that proven methods are being sidelined. Katherine said she understood, wanted balance, and suggested analyzing the data together to integrate both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shared recent digital campaign success stories showing boosted engagement and sales. Bradley heard this, found the results impressive, and asked how those strategies are developed. Katherine said it is about targeting the right audience with the right message and offered to walk him through the analytics/decision-making. Bradley admitted he had doubts about moving away from traditional methods but now wanted to understand digital better. Katherine welcomed his openness and suggested diving deeper into the data.
- Bradley proposed a joint strategy meeting to combine traditional and digital marketing. Katherine agreed. He said he hoped leveraging both their expertise would create something impactful and appreciated her willingness to collaborate. Katherine said she looked forward to it and wanted to leverage each other’s strengths.
- After their joint meeting, Bradley worked overtime preparing a draft board presentation integrating both their ideas. He was excited and told Katherine. Katherine reviewed it, called it comprehensive and well thought out, and said his hard work showed. Bradley thanked her, said he was convinced the integrated approach would set them apart from competitors, and wanted to nail the presentation. Katherine said she was confident and suggested reviewing/fine-tuning once more.
- After their board presentation and implementation, Bradley thanked Katherine, saying he learned much and was grateful for his growth through their collaboration. Katherine said it was a pleasure seeing the project come to fruition and that his openness made it a successful partnership. Bradley proposed regular strategy sessions; Katherine agreed, saying they would keep on top of their game and market trends.

He does **not** have access to Katherine’s private thoughts, unspoken motives, or narrator-only information beyond what she said or did in their interactions.
